slo_title: Close JDBC resources properly to avoid leaks

mcq.q: What will happen if you don’t close the ResultSet and Connection after query execution?

options.C: Memory leak and DB resource exhaustion

mcq.answer_text: Memory leak and DB resource exhaustion

mcq.q: Which Java feature simplifies closing JDBC resources automatically?

Which block is best suited for closing JDBC resources like Connection , Statement , and ResultSet ?
What is the recommended approach to handle SQL exceptions in JDBC code?

options.A: Use throws SQLException in the main method only
options.B: Catch SQLException and log the error
options.C: Ignore exceptions to prevent app termination

mcq.answer_text: Catch SQLException and log the error

sq.q: What is the purpose of the finally block in JDBC resource handling?
answer: The finally block ensures that resources like Connection , Statement , and ResultSet are closed regardless of whether an exception occurs or not, preventing memory/resource leaks.

lq.q: You are developing a Java application that retrieves employee data from a MySQL database. Implement a JDBC program that: Connects to the database Connects to the database Retrieves employee names and salaries from the employees table Retrieves employee names and salaries from the employees table Applies proper exception handling Applies proper exception handling Closes all JDBC resources in the finally block Closes all JDBC resources in the finally block
answer: public class EmployeeData { public static void main(String[] args) { String url = "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/company"; String user = "root"; String pass = "admin"; Connection con = null; Statement stmt = null; ResultSet rs = null;
// Establish Connection con = DriverManager.getConnection(url, user, pass);
// Execute Query rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT name, salary FROM employees");
// Process Results while (rs.next()) { System.out.println("Name: " + rs.getString("name") + ", Salary: " + rs.getDouble("salary")); }

} catch (SQLException e) { System.err.println("Database error: " + e.getMessage()); } catch (ClassNotFoundException e) { System.err.println("Driver not found: " + e.getMessage()); } finally { // Close resources try { if (rs != null) rs.close(); } catch (Exception e) {} try { if (stmt != null) stmt.close(); } catch (Exception e) {} try { if (con != null) con.close(); } catch (Exception e) {} } } }
